reason: The trigger is real and inside the window: on 24 August 2026 Navitas (Nasdaq: NVTS) signed a definitive agreement to acquire Claros, Inc. for up to approximately $232.8 million, about $216.0 million payable at closing in cash and Class A stock (share value struck on the 21 August close of $12.97) and the balance in stock on milestones over the following two years. GaN and silicon-carbide power semiconductors are as close to Formula E's technical core as a component category gets - inverters, DC-DC, on-board and 600kW fast charging - so this looked like a Mode A case. It does not survive the numbers. Q2 2026 revenue was $10.5 million, up 22 per cent sequentially, on a non-GAAP operating loss of about $11.4 million; the company holds $557 million of cash, but roughly $373 million of that was raised in the quarter at an average of $21.89 a share on an AI-infrastructure story. A company at roughly $42 million of annualised revenue, still loss-making, committing to a three-year motorsport sponsorship is not a credible use of that money, and the desk should say so rather than dress a cash balance up as capacity. The second problem is direction of travel: the 'Navitas 2.0' transition, described by the company as substantially complete at Q2, exits mobile and low-end consumer and points the business at AI data centres, grid and energy systems, performance computing and industrial electrification, with AI data centres plus grid and energy expected to be over a third of sales by the end of 2026. The Claros deal is explicitly a 'grid-to-xPU' AI-infrastructure move. The EV audience that makes Formula E worth buying is the half of Navitas's story that is shrinking, not growing. Honest score 68/100 - capacity 12, brand fit 12 - which is under the threshold, and no team lane is worth opening on it. If Navitas ever becomes a motorsport prospect it is a Formula 1 AI-infrastructure one, and the desk already carries 45 Formula 1 signals. Leadership checked: Chris Allexandre, President and CEO since 1 September 2025; Tonya Stevens, CFO from 30 March 2026; Richard Hendrix, Chairman; no chief marketing officer is listed and no motorsport tie was found for any of them.
